issues.description: trainer_args key mismatch: code reads 'max_step' while docstring/config specify 'max_steps'
issues.detail: __init__ reads trainer_args['max_step'] (singular) but the docstring and intended config use 'max_steps' (plural). Callers writing to the documented contract will KeyError. The untyped dict-as-API is the root cause; lift trainer_args into a small dataclass so the data shape and algorithm cannot drift.

issues.description: val_interval is documented but never used; validation actually fires every save_interval
issues.detail: run() calls self.valid() and save_checkpoint unconditionally after each train() block, which exits after save_interval steps. val_interval is advertised in trainer_args but never read. Either drive validation off val_interval or remove the dead knob. One number is silently controlling three different cadences.

issues.description: DeepSpeedTrainer silently depends on a global wandb.run with no precondition check or injection
issues.detail: The docstring warns wandb must be initialized externally, but __init__ mutates wandb.config and run() calls wandb.log with no assert and no injected logger. This hidden global is part of the contract yet invisible at the interface. Inject a logger sink (or a no-op logger on non-zero ranks) so the value flow is explicit and testable.

issues.description: Data specifier strings are a stringly-typed mini-language re-parsed in multiple places
issues.detail: 'task:name:data_json[:factor]' is split with .split() in train.py and re-parsed downstream, with the grammar living only in --help text. Parse once at the CLI boundary into a small dataclass {task, name, path, factor} and pass the value. As written, paths with colons or spaces are silently mishandled.

issues.description: _load_checkpoint conflates filesystem name parsing with stored step and silently falls back on missing resume_path
issues.detail: Discovery globs 'step_*' and sorts by int(name.split('step_')[-1]) while also reading global_step from client_state — two sources of truth, and a renamed directory crashes mid-run. Additionally, an explicit resume_path that does not exist silently falls through to step 0 instead of raising. Use an index file or symlink, and fail loudly on missing explicit paths.

issues.description: _all_reduce_stats has a surprising frame: mutates tensors in place and rebinds dict entries
issues.detail: all_reduce mutates tensors in place, then stats[key] = stats[key] / world_size replaces the entry with a new tensor. Callers holding references see partial mutation and type drift. Return a new dict (or NamedTuple) to make the transform pure and the data flow obvious; async_op buys nothing since every handle.wait() precedes the next use.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on two real bugs and a cluster of structural concerns rooted in the same cause: trainer_args is an untyped dict and the data shape has drifted from the algorithm. P0s are the 'max_step' vs 'max_steps' key mismatch and the unused val_interval knob (validation actually fires every save_interval). P1s cover the hidden wandb global dependency, stringly-typed data specifiers re-parsed everywhere, fragile filename-based checkpoint discovery with a silent missing-path fallback, and the surprising mutate-and-rebind frame in _all_reduce_stats. Lifting trainer_args and specifiers into small typed records and injecting the logger would eliminate most of these in one pass.
